title: A copy through an alias follows the anchor defined last
notes: An alias refers to the most recent preceding node with the same anchor (section 7.1), and an anchor may be redefined (yaml-test-suite 3GZX, PW8X). Here `&b` marks the outer mapping and then the scalar 1 inside it; `copy: *b` comes after both, so it stands for the scalar 1, not the mapping. Copying `/copy` to `/z` writes that value without its anchor, and because the name `b` is defined more than once the alias is written out, not kept as `*b` (docs/edit-semantics.md, copied values); the new member goes at the end of its mapping (docs/edit-semantics.md). Both are kit conventions; a copy of the outer mapping is wrong under any convention.

provenance.reference: A document model that resolved an alias to the first definition of its name, so a copy of `*b` carried the outer mapping.
